(FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND FOUNDATION STUDENTS) 
 
1.  Q: What is Supplementary Examination?  
A: Starting from October 2023 Trimester, the University has conducted Supplementary Examination, by 
giving a second chance to students upon failing their Main Examination. This enables students to 
demonstrate that they have achieved the learning outcome, to pass a course, and to proceed with 
their programme of studies without delay. 
 
2.  Q: Is Supplementary Examination of the same standard and duration as that of the Main Examination? 
A: Yes. Both examinations are of the same standards, duration and expectations.

3.  Q: What are the differences between Supplementary Examination and Replacement Examination? 
A: Supplementary Examination is a second chance given to students upon failing their Main Examination 
and the final marks and grade will be capped at 50 marks or Grade C.  
 
Replacement Examination is a first attempt given to the students after being absent from the Main 
Examination due to justifiable/accepted reasons and the final marks and grade will be the actual marks 
scored (i.e. there is no maximum marks capped at 50 marks or Grade C).  
 
For more details, please refer to the comparison poster between Supplementary Examination and 
Replacement Examination which is available in the Stude

oster between Supplementary Examination and 
Replacement Examination which is available in the Student Portal. 
 
4.  Q: Since the final marks and grade will be capped at 50 marks or Grade C, do I need to answer all the 
questions in the Supplementary Examination?  
A: Yes, you are required to attempt all the required questions as specified in the question papers to obtain 
the best score given this second chance.
